subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Vulvovaginal Pathology, Lichen Sclerosus and Neoplasia

steps.tx: A chronic inflammatory mucocutaneous disorder predominantly affecting postmenopausal women is **vulval lichen sclerosus**. It presents with severe intractable pruritus, ivory-white porcelain plaques, figure-of-eight perianal extension, parchment-like skin wrinkling, and architectural destruction including resorption of the labia minora and clitoral phimosis. First-line medical therapy requires ultra-potent topical corticosteroids like clobetasol propionate.
steps.say: Lichen sclerosus causes severe pruritus, ivory-white plaques, and architectural fusion, responding to topical clobetasol.

left.title: Clinical Manifestations
points: Porcelain white plaques and paper-like skin
Resorption of labia minora and clitoral hooding

steps.tx: Premalignant dysplastic changes of the vulval squamous epithelium are designated **vulval intraepithelial neoplasia**. Current classification separates VIN into two distinct biological pathways: usual-type VIN, driven by oncogenic high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes sixteen and eighteen in younger women, and differentiated VIN, associated with chronic lichen sclerosus, TP53 mutations, and high malignant potential.
steps.say: Vulval intraepithelial neoplasia comprises HPV-associated usual type and lichen sclerosus-linked differentiated type.

steps.tx: Over ninety percent of primary vulval malignancies are **vulval squamous cell carcinoma**, typically presenting as an ulcerated exophytic plaque or persistent pruritic nodule on the labium majus. Initial evaluation requires a full-thickness punch biopsy including subcutaneous tissue. Surgical staging entails radical local excision with generous margins combined with regional inguinofemoral lymph node dissection.
steps.say: Squamous cell carcinoma is the primary vulval cancer and requires radical excision with groin node staging.

vis.alt: FIGO staging of carcinoma of the vulva.
vis.caption: FIGO anatomical stages for vulval carcinoma by tumor size and nodal involvement. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The most significant independent determinant of long-term survival in invasive vulval carcinoma is **inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy**. For unifocal tumors smaller than four centimeters without clinical nodal disease, sentinel lymph node biopsy using technetium-99m and blue dye decreases operative morbidity. Superficial and deep femoral lymph nodes beneath the cribriform fascia must be removed when complete lymphadenectomy is indicated.
steps.say: Inguinofemoral nodal status governs survival, with sentinel lymph node biopsy minimizing lymphedema morbidity.

left.title: Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy
points: Reduces risk of lower limb lymphedema

right.title: Full Inguinofemoral Dissection
points: Multifocal tumors or positive sentinel node
Resection of superficial and deep femoral nodes
Cloquet node sampling at femoral canal

steps.tx: Obstruction of the main excretory duct of the greater vestibular gland produces a **Bartholin gland swelling**. While uninfected cysts present as painless fluctuant swellings at the four or eight o'clock positions of the posterior introitus, secondary infection creates an intensely painful, erythematous, fluctuant Bartholin abscess. Simple needle aspiration or simple incision and drainage results in universal recurrence.
steps.say: Bartholin duct obstruction creates an introital swelling that develops into an abscess when secondarily infected.

steps.tx: The definitive surgical management for recurrent Bartholin cyst or acute abscess is **surgical marsupialisation**. An elliptical incision over the mucosal aspect of the cyst opens the cavity, evacuates purulent contents, and stitches the everted cyst lining to the adjacent vestibular mucosa with interrupted absorbable sutures, creating a permanent epithelialized draining fistula.
steps.say: Marsupialisation everts the cyst wall to construct a permanent drainage channel that prevents recurrence.

vis.alt: Surgical technique of Bartholin cyst marsupialisation.
vis.caption: Surgical marsupialisation of a Bartholin cyst creating an everted drainage tract. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: In utero maternal exposure to the synthetic nonsteroidal estrogen **diethylstilbestrol exposure** is strongly linked to vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma in female offspring. Maternal ingestion during the first trimester causes failure of vaginal müllerian duct transformation, resulting in vaginal adenosis, structural cockscomb cervix, and subsequent clear cell malignant transformation during early adulthood.
steps.say: In utero diethylstilbestrol exposure predisposes female offspring to vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma.

right.title: Neoplastic Consequence
points: Presents in young women aged 15 to 25

steps.tx: A rare pediatric vaginal malignancy occurring almost exclusively in infants and girls under five years of age is **sarcoma botryoides**. This embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma arises in the subepithelial vaginal stroma, producing characteristic grape-like translucent polypoid masses that protrude through the introitus. Histology displays primitive desmin-positive rhabdomyoblasts and a subepithelial cellular cambium layer.
steps.say: Sarcoma botryoides is an embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma presenting with grape-like vaginal masses in young girls.

vis.caption: Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma showing cambium layer and small round blue cells. [Credit: StewardMD]
